list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PlayStation; no online trophies — all 55 unlock in single-player.
method: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published on PlayStation (via Exophase and PSNProfiles, which agree on all 55). Every guide below is written in our own words for this guide. Where a guide goes beyond the official description it says so: 'from the official description' means the advice is our reading of the description and has not yet been checked in the game; 'reported' means a named guide reports it and we cite it. Counts that are not in the official description are only stated where a cited source confirms them; otherwise the guide points at the in-game progress tracker.

EXO.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (official list: names, descriptions, grades)

PSN.name: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (grades and PSN progress targets)

PSQ.name: Push Square — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours — there is nothing extra to do for it. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap, not a task of its own: story first, then the stranger strands, then collectibles and activities, and finally the 100% cleanup. Reported estimates put the whole run at around 200 hours, so pace it and let the checklist do the remembering.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order.
Follow the roadmap stages in this guide: story, strands, collectibles, activities, 100%.
Check the progress bar on the checklist — it counts down to this trophy.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn — just play the story from the start and it unlocks when the mission ends. Because there is reportedly no mission replay, keep a manual save at the start of the chapter anyway; it costs nothing and protects every story trophy below.
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end.
Keep a manual save from before the mission, in case you ever need to replay it.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks at the chapter's end. Nothing here is optional: the chapter trophies are pure progress markers. Save manually at the start of the chapter — with no mission replay reported, a save is the only way back to a missed story beat.
steps: Play through all of Chapter 1's story missions in order.
Save manually at the start of Chapter 1 and again before its final mission.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: The Chapter 2 completion trophy, earned by playing the chapter's story missions to the end. Chapter 2 is also where the map opens up — both protagonists become playable, according to early reports — so this is a good moment to start the side activities that stay open, rather than rushing straight on.
steps: Play through all of Chapter 2's story missions.
Save manually at the start of Chapter 2.
Use the newly opened map to try one or two side activities before moving on.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3's story missions and the trophy is yours at the chapter's close. Keep the manual-save habit: one save at the start of the chapter, one before its last mission. By now the stranger strands and collectibles are worth picking up between missions, since they feed the later roadmap stages.
steps: Play through all of Chapter 3's story missions.
Save manually at the start of Chapter 3.
Between missions, clear any stranger strands or collectibles nearby.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: The Chapter 4 completion trophy, unlocked by finishing the chapter's story missions. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so before the final mission, make a separate manual save — it is the save you will want if any finale-linked trophy goes wrong.
steps: Play through all of Chapter 4's story missions.
Save manually at the start of Chapter 4.
Before the final mission, make a dedicated manual save and keep it.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: One of only two gold trophies: finish the final mission and it unlocks with the credits. This is the trophy the manual-save advice exists for — reported guides say there is no mission replay, so a save from just before the finale is your only way to redo it. After the credits, free roam continues, so the cleanup stages of the roadmap all happen from here.
steps: Load your manual save from before the final mission if anything went wrong earlier.
Complete the final mission.
After the credits, continue in free roam for the roadmap's cleanup stages.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Earned by completing the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies unlock naturally as you play the story — the only thing to get wrong is skipping the mission, which the story does not let you do. Keep a chapter-start save as your safety net.
steps: Play the story until the mission Breakfast Run appears.
Complete it; the trophy unlocks at the mission's end.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Earned by completing the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are story beats, so this unlocks in the natural course of the story. If you are following the roadmap, this is one of the missions to have a manual save in front of.
steps: Play the story until The Cartel Heist unlocks.
Complete the heist mission.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Earned by completing the story mission Child's Play. Like the other mission trophies it comes from playing the story through — no side requirement, no collectible, just the mission itself.
steps: Play the story until the mission Child's Play appears.
Complete it.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Earned by completing the story mission Headliners. A straight story-progress trophy: reach the mission in the story, finish it, and it unlocks.
steps: Play the story until the mission Headliners appears.
Complete it.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Earned by completing the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Finish the mission and the trophy pops. The airport also matters for the Catch Me If You Can trophy, so note the layout while you are there.
steps: Play the story until the mission VCIA Takedown appears.
Complete it.
While at the airport, note the runways and exits for later.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Earned by completing the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The last of the named mission trophies — finish it in the story and it unlocks. Expect a heavier combat mission from the name alone; stock up on armour and ammo before starting, as our own advice from the mission's name, not a confirmed walkthrough.
steps: Play the story until Operation Savage Glory appears.
Stock up on armour and ammo first.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold trophy and the hardest on the list: reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist (Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion). Reported guides say the checklist opens after the story and that nothing on it is missable. What it asks for, as reported by GTABase: all robberies including the 8 bank vaults and the 39 gang operations, underwater discoveries, every Shooting Range gold medal, all drone races, and Bret's 15 Target Decks, plus 70 of the 80 challenges. Work through the checklist itself — it is the authority, and this guide's roadmap stage 5 is built around it.
steps: Finish the story, then open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion.
Clear every line the checklist shows: robberies, vaults, gang operations, underwater finds, shooting ranges, drone races, Target Decks.
Finish 70 of the 80 challenges.
Tick each line off in this guide's checklist as you go.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, airtime and the like, as the game counts them. This is a grind best done passively: drive fast, take jumps and ramps whenever you see them, and the count climbs across the whole playthrough. Save a dedicated stunt session for the end, using the same jump or ramp repeatedly, if the last few dozen drag.
steps: Drive aggressively from the start: jumps, airtime and near misses all count.
Watch the stunt counter in the in-game stats.
Grind the remainder at the end with one repeatable jump.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types once. GTABase lists them as: fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball (sink one basket), an arcade game, winning a race (car race, race challenge or Top Fun drone race), and a stunt. None of them needs to be won or mastered except where stated — one try each is enough, so work through the list early and tick each type off here.
steps: Fish once, hunt once, play one hole of golf.
Visit a shooting range, play pool, sink one basketball shot.
Play one arcade game, win one race of any kind, and pull off one stunt.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Push Square reports two ranges in Leonida — Rodgers Ranch & Shooting Range in Port Gellhorn and Griffin Shooting Range in Balsero — found on the map under Touch Pad, then Activities, then Shooting Ranges. Gold medals are a skill check, not a grind: learn each challenge's rhythm, use the weapon the challenge gives you, and replay the ones you miss. Ranges also raise your Focus level, which helps the Gunslinger trophy.
steps: Open the map: Touch Pad > Activities > Shooting Ranges to find both ranges.
Play every challenge and chase gold, not just a pass.
Replay missed challenges; your best medal per challenge is what counts.
42 gold medals across both ranges unlocks the trophy.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations — one win per location is enough for this trophy. GTABase reports there are 42 drone races in total across those locations, and the 100% checklist wants all of them, so while you are at a location it is worth finishing its other races too rather than coming back later.
steps: Find a Top Fun location on the map and enter its drone race.
Win one race at each of the 14 locations.
While there, clear the location's remaining races for the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — each race only counts once, so you need variety, not repeats of one easy win. GTABase reports there are 40 races to choose from. Mix car races, race challenges and drone races, and spread them across the playthrough so the wins accumulate naturally.
steps: Enter races from the map and race markers.
Win 20 different ones; repeats of the same race do not count twice.
Drone race wins count too — they can fill gaps.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are head-to-head: out-fish Cal and the trophy is yours. As our own advice from the description, pick a challenge when you are comfortable with the fishing controls, keep your line steady, and reel in smoothly rather than yanking — the exact rules are not yet confirmed in the game, so treat the first attempt as practice.
steps: Find Cal and take his fishing challenge.
Learn the fishing controls first if you have not fished before.
Out-fish Cal to win the challenge.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish it, not just start it. Arcade cabinets are scattered around Leonida; walk up to one, play it through to its end, and the trophy unlocks. This also ticks one of the 9 activity types for Master of None.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet.
Play the game to its end.
If you fail, try again — completion is what counts.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's strand. Contact strands are the game's side stories: take Andy's missions whenever they appear and follow the strand to its last mission. This guide does not yet confirm whether contact strands stay open after the finale, so do not leave Andy's last mission sitting unfinished for long.
steps: Take Andy's missions as they appear.
Follow the strand to its final mission and complete it.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's strand. Like the other contact trophies, this is a strand to follow to its end: take Kenton's missions when they come up and finish the last one. Do not assume the strand waits forever — clear it while you are working through the contacts.
steps: Take Kenton's missions as they appear.
Follow the strand to its final mission and complete it.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's strand. Work through Billy's missions in order until the strand ends with its final mission. One of five contact-finale trophies — clearing all five strands is a whole roadmap stage of its own.
steps: Take Billy's missions as they appear.
Follow the strand to its final mission and complete it.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the classic GTA side-mission hunt. Stranger missions appear as icons on the map; take them, follow each strand to its end, and count them here. Eight strands is a lot of driving around the state, so pick them up whenever you pass one rather than saving them all for the end.
steps: Watch the map for stranger mission icons.
Complete 8 full strands, not just 8 single missions.
Track each finished strand in this checklist.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's strand. Take Randy's missions as they appear and follow the strand through to its last mission. Clear the contact strands in the same playthrough sweep as the stranger strands — they overlap in how you find them.
steps: Take Randy's missions as they appear.
Follow the strand to its final mission and complete it.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's strand — the last of the five contact-finale trophies. With Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone all finished, the contacts stage of the roadmap is done.
steps: Take Tyrone's missions as they appear.
Follow the strand to its final mission and complete it.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet scenic places; visit each one and meditate there, and the trophy unlocks at the last one. The total number of spots is not yet confirmed by a cited source, so use the in-game tracker to see how many remain — this guide will not state a count it cannot cite.
steps: Find meditation spots while exploring — scenic viewpoints and quiet places.
Meditate at each one.
Check the in-game tracker for how many spots remain.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a specific creature, not just any hunt. Take Bret's hunt, track the unique animal, and bring it down. Hunting also ticks one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, and Bret's Target Decks feed the 100% checklist, so his strand is worth following properly.
steps: Take Bret's hunting mission.
Track the unique animal — follow its signs, do not just wander.
Take it down to complete the hunt.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — find every card in three full sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida; each set needs all of its cards, so collect as you explore and use the in-game tracker to see which sets are close to complete. Bret's Target Decks are a related 100% item, so card hunting doubles up with the cleanup stage.
steps: Pick up collectible cards wherever you find them while exploring.
Watch the tracker to see which sets are nearest complete.
Finish 3 full sets.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 locations across Leonida — a pure exploration grind. The trick is habit: WAiNK at every new place you stop, not just the obvious landmarks, and the count climbs with your normal travel. Check the in-game tracker to see how many locations remain.
steps: WAiNK at every new location you visit, as a habit.
Sweep the map region by region for places you have not WAiNKed.
100 locations unlocks the trophy.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small goals scattered through activities and exploration — GTABase reports there are 80 in total, and the 100% checklist wants 70 of them, so this trophy's 50 is a milestone on the way to the bigger target. Work through the challenge list in the game and clear the easy ones first.
steps: Open the challenges list in the game.
Clear the easiest 50 first.
Keep going to 70 for the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape. Do it somewhere you can run: cause enough trouble to reach 4 stars, then break line of sight, get out of the search area and stay hidden until the stars clear. Your partner must be with you when the heat drops — do not leave them behind.
steps: Bring your partner along.
Raise your wanted level to 4 stars.
Break line of sight and escape the search area until the stars clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level — the tricky part is the 'without losing it': you must keep the heat on through all three robberies. Plan a route of three close shops, hit them one after another with your partner, and do not let the stars drop between them. If the wanted level clears, start the count again.
steps: Pick three shops close together and plan the route.
Rob them one after another with your partner.
Keep the wanted level alive through all three — if it drops, restart.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — drive or find 100 different ones. Variety is the point: every new model you get into counts, so try everything you see parked or driving past, from scooters to trucks. The in-game vehicle tracker shows what you have found and what is left.
steps: Get into every new vehicle model you see.
Try different districts — different areas have different traffic.
100 distinct vehicles unlocks the trophy.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — one slow-motion window, five downs. Set it up: find a spot with at least five enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them fast with headshots. The shooting ranges raise your Focus level, which makes this easier, so do The Shootist work first if you are struggling.
steps: Find a fight with 5 or more enemies grouped together.
Trigger Combat Focus and down 5 before it ends.
If you fall short, raise your Focus level at the shooting ranges and retry.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — in plain words, steal a plane and take off without a ticket. Get onto the airfield, find a plane, and get airborne. Expect airport security to object; a fast plane and a quick takeoff matter more than a fight.
steps: Get into VCIA and reach the airfield.
Take a plane and take off.
Get clear of the airport to seal it.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: A hidden trophy whose description is a joke, not an instruction: 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos.' The Rhino is the game's tank, so this is about doing something notable in one — surviving in it, using it, or taking heat in it, as our own reading of the description. This guide does not invent a specific method: get into a Rhino, use it in combat, and watch for the pop. The exact trigger is not yet confirmed by a cited source.
steps: Find a Rhino tank.
Use it in combat and stay in it under fire.
If it does not pop, try a longer stint in the tank.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery. Case the store first: learn the guards' and cameras' patterns, move quietly, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. Being spotted at any point fails the condition, so patience beats speed; if you are detected, leave and try again.
steps: Pick a jewelry store and watch its guards and cameras.
Move quietly, take the goods, and leave unseen.
If detected, abandon the attempt and retry.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — five separate vault jobs, each ending with a clean getaway. Plan each one: a fast car parked close, a route out, and no lingering at the scene. GTABase reports the 100% checklist wants 8 vaults in total, so this trophy's 5 is a milestone — keep going to 8 for A Long Road.
steps: Find a bank vault and rob it.
Escape cleanly after each robbery.
Repeat for 5 vaults — then continue to 8 for the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run routes around Leonida — intercept one, stop it, take its cargo and get away before the response arrives. A roadblock or a well-placed ram works to stop it; a fast getaway car parked nearby works to leave.
steps: Find an armored truck on its route.
Stop it and take the cargo.
Escape before the response closes in.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — visit every area of the map. The game tracks which areas you have been to, so sweep the map systematically: coast, city, swamps and countryside, region by region, until the tracker shows nothing left. Pair this with the WAiNK and meditation sweeps so one trip covers three trophies.
steps: Open the map and note the regions you have not visited.
Travel through each one — driving through counts as exploring.
Check the in-game tracker for areas left.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — one per gang, across all of them. Gang operations are marked around the map; hit one operation for every gang in the state. GTABase reports 39 gang operations in total, and the 100% checklist wants all of them, so this trophy is the first pass — keep hitting operations until the checklist is clear.
steps: Find gang illegal operations on the map.
Rob one operation for each gang.
Keep going to all 39 operations for the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — find a bar or vendor on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and drink it where you can see the water. A small moment trophy: go to the beachfront, buy the drink, and let the scene play. No fighting, no grind — just the view.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Find a place serving cocktails on the beachfront.
Order one and drink it with the view.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out onto the street, the way the old games taught us. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or pointed at it, and floor it through the window. 'Classic style' means do it loud and in a car, not on foot.
steps: Find a vehicle showroom.
Get a car lined up on its glass front.
Drive straight through and out onto the street.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — go bowling there. Find the alley, start a game, and bowl: the trophy is about playing it through, not about a perfect score. This also helps with the activity list for Master of None if bowling counts as one of its types — the 9 types GTABase lists do not include bowling, so treat this as its own trophy.
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a game and bowl through it.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A hidden trophy with a cryptic description: 'A partnership with mass appeal.' Our reading, from the description alone: something you do with your partner that draws a crowd or goes public — a shared moment with an audience. This guide will not invent a method: play the partner content, watch for moments with a crowd, and the exact trigger is still to be confirmed by a cited source.
steps: Play partner content and look for public, crowd-drawing moments.
Try activities together where an audience is present.
Check back here — this entry will be updated when a source confirms the trigger.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: A story trophy about choices: 'Choices made (for better or worse).' PSN tracks a count for it, reportedly up to 500, which suggests it is about making choices across the game rather than one single decision. Our advice from the description: do not rush past choice moments — engage with them as they come, and keep your chapter-start manual saves, because with no mission replay a choice you regret may be locked in. Flagged missable for exactly that reason.
steps: Engage with choice moments as they appear in the story.
Keep manual saves at the start of each chapter.
Do not skip dialogue choices — they are the content here.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: A hidden trophy: 'Second time's the charm.' Our reading, from the description alone: succeed at something on the second attempt after failing it once. That could be a mission, a challenge or an activity — the description does not say which. This guide will not invent a trigger: play normally, retry what you fail, and this is likely to pop on its own. The exact trigger is still to be confirmed by a cited source.
steps: Play normally and retry anything you fail.
If it has not popped by the endgame, retry a failed challenge deliberately.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: A hidden trophy: 'What the hell just happened?' Our reading, from the description alone: witness something strange — an easter egg, a weird encounter, something out of the ordinary in Leonida. These moments are usually found by exploring odd places at odd times. This guide will not invent a location: explore, pay attention to strange sights, and the exact trigger is still to be confirmed by a cited source.
steps: Explore unusual places across Leonida.
Investigate anything strange you see.
Check back here when a source confirms the trigger.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a pedestrian with a melee weapon while driving past. Get a melee weapon, find a pedestrian on a roadside, drive by slowly and swing as you pass. It is a precision trick, not a brawl: one clean hit while moving is the whole trophy. Pick a quiet road so you are not fighting the police at the same time.
steps: Equip a melee weapon.
Find a pedestrian beside a quiet road.
Drive past and land the melee hit while moving.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies and heists; your contacts clean them for a cut. Keep the loop going: rob, launder, repeat, and the total climbs. It pairs naturally with the robbery trophies — the same jobs that feed Maximum Withdrawal feed this one.
steps: Collect marked bills from robberies and heists.
Launder them through your contacts.
Repeat until $250,000 is laundered.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, cars, food, anything sold in a shop counts toward one total. This is a passive trophy if you play normally: buy the gear you want and the total climbs. If it lags behind at the end, spend the surplus on the most expensive items you can find.
steps: Buy what you need as you play — it all counts.
Check the spending total in the stats.
At the end, spend any surplus on big-ticket items.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — buy every garage the game sells. Garages are properties on the map; visit each one for sale and buy it. The total number is not yet confirmed by a cited source, so use the in-game property list to see what is left rather than a number from this guide. Save the money for it as you go — garages are not cheap.
steps: Find garages for sale on the map.
Buy each one.
Check the property list for any you have not bought.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the in-game delivery app: register vehicles you find to it, ten in total. It pairs with Whip It Good — the vehicles you discover for that trophy are candidates to register here, so register as you discover.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app.
Register vehicles you find — ten in total.
Register new discoveries as you go, alongside the vehicle hunt.
